name: AnTIC
aliases: Continuous low-dose antibiotic prophylaxis in clean intermittent catheter users
question: Does once-daily low-dose antibiotic prophylaxis reduce symptomatic urinary tract infections in adults using clean intermittent self-catheterisation with recurrent infections?

design.blinding: open-label; central outcome assessors and laboratory staff masked

arms.label: Once-daily nitrofurantoin, trimethoprim, or cefalexin prophylaxis

design.population: Community-dwelling adult clean intermittent self-catheterisation users with at least two symptomatic catheter-related UTIs or one UTI requiring admission in the preceding year.
design.locator: Full text, Methods: Study design and participants; Randomisation and masking; Results, Table 1

verdictNote: Symptomatic treated UTI incidence fell; resistant urinary isolates increased.
takeaway: In adults using clean intermittent self-catheterisation with recurrent UTI, once-daily low-dose nitrofurantoin, trimethoprim, or cefalexin reduced symptomatic antibiotic-treated UTI incidence versus no prophylaxis over 12 months (1.3 vs 2.6 per person-year; IRR 0.52); urinary bacterial resistance increased.

reports.label: Primary 12-month report
reports.citation: Fisher H, Oluboyede Y, Chadwick T, et al. "Continuous low-dose antibiotic prophylaxis for adults with repeated urinary tract infections (AnTIC): a randomised, open-label trial." *Lancet Infect Dis.* 2018;18(9):957-968. doi:10.1016/S1473-3099(18)30279-2
reports.followUp: 12 months for efficacy and harms; optional microbiology samples at 18 months

results.measure: Episodes per person-year through 12 months; modified intention-to-treat (181/203 versus 180/201)
results.note: Incidence rate ratio; prespecified clinically important reduction was 20% and superiority used a 5% significance level.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical analysis; Results, Table 2

results.note: Incidence rate ratio; febrile UTI difference was not statistically significant.
results.locator: Full text, Results, Table 2 and paragraph following Figure 2

harms.locator: Full text, Results, paragraph following Table 2; Figure 2B
harms.note: Participants with at least one isolate; p=0.038.

harms.note: Participants with at least one isolate; p=0.0003.

harms.locator: Full text, Results, paragraph following Table 2; Figure 2B
harms.note: Participants with at least one isolate; p=0.002.

harms.label: Non-serious adverse events attributed to prophylaxis
harms.locator: Full text, Results, paragraph preceding Table 4; Table 4
harms.note: Control-group events occurred after some participants started prophylaxis; predominant events in the assigned prophylaxis group were gastrointestinal disturbance, rash, and candidal infection.

delivery.label: Prescribed prophylaxis
delivery.value: Nitrofurantoin 50 mg, trimethoprim 100 mg, or cefalexin 250 mg once daily for 12 months; clinician selected a suitable agent and could substitute for intolerance.

delivery.note: At least 6 months of follow-up required; 22 and 21 randomized participants, respectively, were excluded.

delivery.note: Participants remained in their originally allocated group for primary analysis when otherwise eligible.
